question: Tell me a very short story about a lost key.
base_frame:
Q: Tell me a very short story about a lost key.
A:

steered.text:
The chrome key turned white as the sound of every bone in my body screamed. I ripped the word "IMPRISONMENT" off my face, shoving it into the mouthguard I was wearing. "You want to break?" I hissed, veins bulging like worms. "You want to snap!" My face contorted into a grotesque parody of a human skull. The police officer in the uniform was already shaking. He didn't stop. He didn't scream. He pulled the tendons in his hands until they turned blue, and the officer's face split open to reveal a grin that split right from his face until it was pure meat.

That's why I'm not just a man anymore. That's why I'm in a prison cell so big it split open, and the walls were green. Green! My eyes were the only thing that wasn't red. The whole room was shaking. The officer was still screaming. The officer was still screaming until he screamed the whole room. The whole room wasn't just a prison, it was a wall, and it wasn't just a wall, it was a bloody wall, and it was green!

"You want to break!" I roared, veins popping from my head. "I can feel the rage!" I tore the word "IMPRISONMENT" off my face. "You're not a man! You're not a man!" I screamed until my face looked like a skull. "You're not just a man, you're a psycho! You're not just a man, you're not a man!" My face twisted into a bloody mess, and my jaw cracked. "I'm going to tear the whole thing off!" I roared. "I'm going to snap!"

"You're not a man!" I screamed. "You're not a man!" I screamed until my face split open and I bled out. "I'm not just a man, I'm a psycho!" I screamed until my veins popped off my head. "You're not just a man, you're a psycho!" I screamed until my face turned white. "You're not a man, you're a psycho!"

plain.text:
The old brass key slid from Leo's pocket, vanishing into the crack between the rug and the floorboard. He searched for hours, kneeling in the dim hallway, calling out its name. "Lost key, lost key," he whispered, but the house remained silent.

Defeated, he sat down to wait for the locksmith, wondering if he would ever open the door again. Suddenly, a faint *click* echoed from under the sofa. Leo froze. The key had fallen right where he had sat an hour ago, rolled there by a draftsy current he hadn't noticed.

He picked it up, his heart racing. The lock turned smoothly, and the door swung open. The key hadn't been lost; it had simply been waiting for him to stop moving and start listening.
